Devices on the LAN can reach the container engine over HTTP. Use only on trusted networks.
Remote control is part of the template pack. Unlock it to manage images, containers and stacks from your browser.
Paused: the template pack is not unlocked, so the web console is not running.
Toggle off/on after changing the port to apply
docker CLI / Portainer cannot send a token: this port is unauthenticated. Trusted LAN only.
Off: this port only accepts connections from this device (adb forward still works). On: any device on the same network can control containers without authentication.

The Docker API port carries no authentication (docker CLI cannot send tokens). With LAN access on, every device on this network can create, start and run commands in your containers. Only continue on a trusted private network.
Export runtime logs and send them to the developer to help diagnose issues.
Keep containers running in the background

Android and especially Chinese vendor ROMs stop background apps aggressively. Containers and the Docker service keep running only when the app is allowed to stay in the background. Complete the three steps below (you can change them later in Settings).
Show the persistent notification of the keep-alive foreground service (required on Android 13+).
Exempt the app from Doze and battery restrictions so containers keep running with the screen off.
Open your system\'s background settings and allow this app to auto-start and run in the background.
You can review these settings anytime in Settings → Background running. Containers keep running while the keep-alive notification is visible.
While containers are running, the app hosts a foreground service to keep them alive. Chinese vendor ROMs still need the permissions below.
Battery optimization: NOT exempted, background containers may be stopped
